title: Balance the bridge

brief.story: Two dividers side by side make a bridge: a sensor circuit that reads zero when its two sides agree. The left side is built. The right side is missing its bottom resistor.
brief.goal: Pick R4 so the two taps (column 8 and column 16) are within 0.1 V of each other: the meter across the bridge reads zero.

hints: Each side is a divider. The left tap sits at 9 V × 2.2 kΩ ÷ (1 kΩ + 2.2 kΩ) = 6.19 V.
The right tap reaches the same voltage when its ratio matches: R4 ÷ R3 = R2 ÷ R1 = 2.2.
10 kΩ × 2.2 = 22 kΩ. Put it from column 16 to the − rail.
debrief: A bridge balances when both sides divide the supply in the same ratio: R2 ÷ R1 = R4 ÷ R3, so both taps sit at 9 V × 2.2 ÷ 3.2 = 6.19 V and the meter between them reads 0 V. That's why bridges are used for sensors: swap R4 for a strain gauge or a thermistor, and the tiniest change in it unbalances the bridge, showing up as a voltage that started from zero.
